title: PUK vs. Mooren’s Ulcer: The Peripheral Melt Masterclass
summary: A high-stakes clinical distinction between life-threatening systemic vasculitis (PUK) and a relentless, idiopathic autoimmune keratitis (Mooren’s). This guide provides a textbook-level breakdown of diagnosis, systemic workup, and aggressive management strategies.

rows: Peripheral corneal thinning with an overlying epithelial defect, associated with stromal infiltration and systemic autoimmune disease.
A rare, idiopathic, relentlessly progressive peripherally-located ulcerative keratitis that occurs in the absence of any detectable systemic disease.
Strictly limited to the cornea; Sclera is characteristically spared.

sections.title: Epidemiology & Demographics
content: PUK: Most common in 5th-7th decades; No gender predilection.
Mooren's Type 1: Typically elderly patients, usually unilateral, responds well to treatment.
Mooren's Type 2: Younger patients (20s-30s), often bilateral, aggressive, poor prognosis.
Mooren's Type 2 is more prevalent in parts of Africa and India.
PUK incidence is tied to the prevalence of systemic RA (approx 3/million/year).

sections.title: Clinical Features Checklist
content: Crescent-shaped peripheral stromal ulceration.
Undermining 'overhanging' leading edge (Pathognomonic for Mooren's).
Epithelial defect over the area of thinning.
Vascularization up to the base of the ulcer.
Severe pain, photophobia, and lacrimation.
Progresses circumferentially and then centrally.
Stromal loss can lead to descemetocele or perforation.

sections.title: RED FLAGS: Ocular Emergencies
content: Presence of PUK may indicate active, life-threatening systemic vasculitis (Mortality up to 40% if untreated).
Sudden decrease in pain (may indicate impending perforation).
Positive Seidel test in the area of thinning.
Co-existing Scleritis: Signifies a much more aggressive systemic process.
Rapid circumferential progression (Full 360-degree 'Stage-Coach Wheel' melt).

sections.title: Mandatory Diagnostic Workup
content: Step 1: Detailed review of systems (joints, skin, respiratory, renal).
Step 2: Serology (RF, anti-CCP, ANA, ANCA, ESR, CRP).
Step 3: Infectious screen (Syphilis, Hep B/C, HIV, Quantiferon Gold).
Step 4: Chest X-ray (GPA, Sarcoidosis, TB).
Step 5: Urinalysis (to look for RBC casts/hematuria in Vasculitis).
Step 6: Corneal scraping (to rule out infectious keratitis).

branches: Catarrhal Keratitis (Staph Hypersensitivity, Clear space to limbus)

sections.title: Management Strategy: Step-Ladder Approach
content: 1. Aggressive Lubrication & Prophylactic Antibiotics (Moxifloxacin).
2. Topical Steroids (Pred Forte 1%) - Use with caution in PUK, more useful in Mooren's.
3. Systemic Corticosteroids (Prednisone 1mg/kg/day) for immediate control.
4. Steroid-Sparing Immunomodulatory Therapy (IMT): Methotrexate, Mycophenolate, or Azathioprine.
5. Cytotoxic Agents: Cyclophosphamide (Gold Standard for GPA/PAN related PUK).
6. Biologics: Rituximab (anti-CD20) or Infliximab (anti-TNFα) for refractory cases.
7. Surgical Intervention if perforation is imminent or medical therapy fails.

sections.title: Surgical Techniques & Interventions
content: Conjunctival Resection/Recession: Removes source of inflammatory cytokines/MMPs (Primarily for Mooren's).
Cyanoacrylate Tissue Adhesive: For small perforations (<2mm) or extreme thinning.
Amniotic Membrane Transplantation (AMT): Multi-layered to provide a biological scaffold.
Lamellar Patch Graft: To restore tectonic integrity.
Tarsorrhaphy: To reduce evaporative stress and promote epithelial healing.

content.explanation: M: Mooren's is Marginal and Mostly Idiopathic. O: Overhanging edge is key. O: Only Cornea (Sclera spared). R: Resect Conjunctiva. P: PUK is Painful and Perilous (Systemic). U: Underlying Vasculitis. K: Keep checking the ANCA/RF.

sections.title: Recent Advances & Landmark Studies
content: The use of Rituximab has shown superior results in GPA-related PUK compared to Cyclophosphamide in recent trials.
Topical Ciclosporin (1% or 2%) and Tacrolimus (0.03%) are increasingly used as adjuncts to reduce systemic steroid load.
Identification of Calgranulin C as a potential autoantigen in Mooren's Ulcer may lead to targeted biological therapies.
The importance of 'early hit' therapy: Initiating IMT within weeks of diagnosis improves 5-year survival rates in PUK patients.

sections.title: Clinical Pearls for the Fellow
content: Never diagnose Mooren's Ulcer without a negative systemic workup.
In PUK, the ocular inflammation is often a barometer for systemic disease activity.
If a patient with RA develops PUK, their 5-year mortality risk increases significantly without systemic immunosuppression.
Avoid topical steroids in Mooren's if the stroma is extremely thin, as they can inhibit collagen synthesis and accelerate melting.
Oral Doxycycline (100mg BID) is a useful adjunct for its anti-collagenolytic (MMP-inhibitor) properties.
